title: Kantele (Finnish plucked zither)
summary: The kantele is a small plucked zither from Finland, hollowed from a block of wood and strung with five strings that run to a bar of tuning pegs. Its bright, ringing tone was made for sung stories, lullabies and dance tunes.
howToPlay: Five strings stand side by side, low on the left and high on the right; each one is a lane.
A bead runs down a string toward the plucking place. Pluck that string just as the bead arrives.
Begin with the five-beat story line, then try the lullaby in three, the dance tune and the drone-and-turn.
Let each note ring on. A stroke between beats blurs the sound, so wait for the next bead.
rules: The five strings are tuned to D, E, F, G and A, a small diatonic set.
A five-beat line is felt as three beats and two, the pulse of old story singing.
A pluck on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and an extra pluck costs points.
Every tune is played through twice.
heritageNote: In Finland and Karelia the kantele has been made and played for many centuries, carved by hand and carried from village to village to accompany singers. Later makers added strings and levers, and today it is taught in schools and concert halls alike.
credits: Tradition: the Finnish kantele; melodies written for this game
